docs.title: Coming soon
docs.text: What's on the way for Printer Buddy. No dates yet — these land as they're ready.

docs.title: Full remote access
docs.text: Open all of Printer Buddy from anywhere, with a login. Today, remote access is share links.

docs.title: More printers
docs.text: Klipper is supported today. Support for more printers is being added over time.

docs.title: 32-bit AI
docs.text: A 32-bit version of the lite AI model, so AI detection works on 32-bit systems too. Today the AI needs a 64-bit system.

docs.title: A printer shows offline
docs.text:
• Check the printer is on and its Moonraker is running (open Fluidd/Mainsail on it).
  • Check Printer Buddy's host can reach it: same network, right IP and port (usually 7125).
  • If Moonraker has login turned on, the printer needs its API key in Printer Buddy.

docs.title: Klipper errors
docs.text: The red banner on the printer page shows Klipper's error. Fix what it says (often a typo in printer.cfg), then press Restart. If Klipper isn't connected at all, try Restart service, then look at klippy.log (link in the banner).

docs.title: An update failed
docs.text:
• The Updates list shows the error. Try again — a dropped connection is the usual cause.
  • If it says to run the installer's Update, do that once: ./install.sh → 3) Update.
  • Still stuck? Reset the code to the latest release and update again:
cd printer-buddy
git fetch origin
git reset --hard origin/$(git branch --show-current)
./update.sh

This only resets the code. Your printers and settings in data/ and printer-buddy.env aren't touched.

docs.title: Port already in use
docs.text: Something else took port 8080. Run ./install.sh, pick P) Change port and choose a free one.

docs.title: Logs
docs.text: Log Where Printer Buddy journalctl -u printer-buddy -f on Printer Buddy's host, or 5) Show logs in the installer Klipper klippy.log — link in the error banner Moonraker moonraker.log — link in the warnings banner

docs.title: Repos
docs.text:
Repo What's in it printer-buddy Core app, installer, AI runtime; all releases are published here print-buddy-ui The web interface print-buddy-notify Notifications print-buddy-timelapse Timelapses print-buddy-streamer Camera streamer print-buddy-relay Cloudflare worker for remote access printer-buddy-docs These docs

The installer downloads the parts into the main checkout: ui/, app/core/notify.py, app/media/timelapse.py and streamer/ (all gitignored).

docs.title: Branches
docs.text:
• nightly — the default branch in the core, UI, notify and streamer repos, where development happens.
  • main — stable. The release workflow moves it forward when a version is released, so don't commit to it. The timelapse, relay and docs repos only have main.

docs.title: Running it locally
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/printer-buddy/printer-buddy.git
cd printer-buddy
python3 app/core/updater.py parts      # download the parts
python3 -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install -r requirements.txt
.venv/bin/uvicorn app.main:app --port 8080

docs.title: Parts
docs.text:
Each part repo (UI, notify, streamer, timelapse) has a release workflow that publishes into the main repo. Run it from Actions → release → Run workflow, on the repo's default branch. The form asks:

Box What it does What to publish stable or nightly Version Stable only. Leave it blank for the next version, or type one like 1.2.5. A version that already exists rolls main back to it When the version is blank, raise the last one by x.x.0 -> x.x.1 (a fix), x.0.0 -> x.1.0 (a new feature) or 0.0.0 -> 1.0.0 (a big change) Test run Does everything except publish, and shows the version and the notes in the run summary
  • Nightly — built every day at 06:00 UTC (only if the part has a new commit), as <part>-nightly. Choosing nightly by hand rebuilds it right away.
  • Stable — checks the code, works out the next version from the last v tag, and asks GitHub Copilot to write the release notes from the commits. If Copilot fails it uses the plain list of commit messages. It then moves main to match the default branch, tags the repo vX.Y.Z, and publishes <part>-vX.Y.Z into the main repo and vX.Y.Z in the part's own repo.

The workflows publish into the main repo with the MAIN_REPO_TOKEN secret. The organization only accepts fine-grained tokens that last 366 days or less, so make a new one before it runs out.

docs.title: needs.txt
docs.text:
If a part needs a minimum version of another part, add needs.txt to its repo, one per line:

streamer v1.4

Updates are held back ("Waiting") until that's met.

docs.title: Core
docs.text:
Run Actions → release → Run workflow from nightly. It has the same version, raise-by and Test run boxes as the parts, but no What to publish box, because core has no nightly release: nightly installs follow the nightly branch itself.

It checks the code (compiles the Python and checks the shell scripts), moves main to match nightly, publishes the release core-vX.Y.Z with Copilot-written notes (the plain commit list is the fallback), and then rebuilds updates.txt. A version that already exists rolls main back to it instead. Stable installs follow main.

docs.title: AI models
docs.text: export.py --release in the AI repo publishes ai-<kind>-vX and starts the ai stats workflow, which tests the models and adds a Model check section to the release notes.

docs.title: updates.txt
docs.text: The updates list workflow rebuilds updates.txt from all releases whenever one is published, and uploads it to the updates release. Printer Buddy reads it to know what's newest.

docs.title: updater.py
docs.text:
app/core/updater.py does every update. The installer, update.sh and the Updates list all call it.

python3 app/core/updater.py update     # core, then everything below
python3 app/core/updater.py parts      # download the parts
python3 app/core/updater.py ai         # AI libraries and model
python3 app/core/updater.py streamer   # download and set up the camera streamer
python3 app/core/updater.py packages   # system packages the chosen features need

It only uses Python's standard library, so it works before the virtual environment exists.

docs.title: Root helper
docs.text:
tools/root.sh is installed as /usr/local/lib/printer-buddy/root.sh, with a sudo rule that lets the Printer Buddy user run only that script without a password. Its jobs:

Job What it does pkg <name> Install an apt package, only from a fixed list (ffmpeg, v4l-utils, ustreamer, python3-venv) deps, unit, enable, restart, disable Set up and control the camera streamer service reboot, shutdown Reboot or power off Printer Buddy's host

The installer updates the helper; the app can't change it.

docs.title: Channels
docs.text:
Setting Meaning PB_CHANNEL stable or nightly for everything PB_NIGHTLY Parts on dev/beta builds, e.g. ui,streamer

Core follows the main branch on stable and nightly on nightly.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
There are two ways to install Printer Buddy. Either way it talks to each printer's Moonraker over the network, and the install steps are the same.

On a printerOn a dedicated host

Install it on the printer's own Klipper host (the Pi or board running Klipper and Moonraker).

Good for: one printer, or a small setup where you don't want a dedicated host.

You need:

  • A printer running Klipper + Moonraker on Debian-based Linux (most Pi-based printers, MainsailOS, FluiddPi…)
  • SSH access to it, plus git and python3

Good to know:

  • The installer adds printer-buddy to Moonraker's service list, so you can restart it from Fluidd or Mainsail too.
  • Port 8080 is often taken by the printer's webcam — the installer then offers the next free port.
  • Keep it light: AI basic at most.

Install it on a dedicated host on the same network as your printers — a Raspberry Pi, a NAS, a home server or an old PC.

Good for: several printers, AI heavy, timelapses of every printer, or cameras plugged into the host.

You need:

  • A host running Debian-based Linux (Raspberry Pi OS 64-bit, Debian, Ubuntu…)
  • git and python3 (the installer adds python3-venv if it's missing)
  • Printers running Klipper + Moonraker on the same network

docs.title: How heavy is it?
docs.text:
Readings from real setups. More coming as members send theirs.

Host Setup Printers Memory CPU idle CPU printing Disk Raspberry Pi 4 — — — — — — Raspberry Pi 5 — — — — — — On a printer — — — — — — x86 PC / server — — — — — —

AI detection needs 64-bit

The AI models need a 64-bit system (aarch64 or x86_64). On a Pi, use Raspberry Pi OS (64-bit). Everything else works on 32-bit, and a 32-bit version of the lite AI model is planned.

docs.title: Install it
docs.text:
Same for both: SSH in and run

git clone https://github.com/printer-buddy/printer-buddy.git
cd printer-buddy
./install.sh

The first time you run it, the installer welcomes you and walks through the setup choices one at a time, from Step 1 of 7 to Step 7 of 7 (see Install choices). Enter keeps the suggested answer for any step. At the end it asks Install Printer Buddy now? [Y/n].

After that, every run opens a menu. Pick 1) Install to install or reinstall, 2) Change setup to change a choice, and so on. To install with the defaults and no questions:

./install.sh -y

It sets up a Python environment, downloads the parts you picked, creates the printer-buddy service and starts it. When it's done it prints the address, usually:

http://<its-ip>:8080

Nightly for now

The guided first run is on nightly and comes to stable with the next release. On stable, 1) Install installs with the default choices. Use 2) Change setup to change them first, or afterwards.

docs.title: Adding printers
docs.text:
1. Open Printer Buddy and click Scan network. It checks your local network for Moonraker (ports 7125 and 80, plus Moonraker's own network announcement). It only lists printers — it doesn't connect to any yet.
  2. Tick the printers you want and click Add selected.
  3. If a printer's Moonraker has login turned on, enter its API key when asked.

Printer not found? Use Add by IP and type its address (and port, if it isn't 7125).

docs.title: Port
docs.text:
Printer Buddy uses port 8080. If something else already has it (often the webcam streamer on Klipper boxes), the installer says what's using it and offers the next free port.

Change it later with P) Change port in the installer menu, or:

./install.sh -y --port 8081

docs.title: Install choices
docs.text:
The installer asks these when you install, and you can change them later with 2) Change setup. They're saved in printer-buddy.env in the Printer Buddy folder.

Choice Options (first = default) Interface advanced (basic is coming soon) AI detection off, basic, heavy Video snapshots, live, timelapse Notifications basic, advanced Remote access off, on Camera streamer off, light, basic, advanced Release channel stable, nightly

docs.title: Interface
docs.text:
• advanced — dashboard, Quick View, each printer's status page, plus Control, Console, Files, History, list view and printer groups.
  • basic — coming soon. It shows greyed out in the menu and can't be picked yet.

docs.title: AI detection
docs.text:
• off — no failure detection.
  • basic — light model that runs on a Pi.
  • heavy — bigger, more accurate model; needs a strong PC or a GPU.

See AI failure detection.

docs.title: Video
docs.text:
• snapshots — camera pictures, refreshed every few seconds.
  • live — smooth live stream.
  • timelapse — live stream plus a timelapse of every print (installs ffmpeg).

docs.title: Notifications
docs.text:
• basic — ntfy or Discord when prints start, pause, finish or fail.
  • advanced — basic plus Telegram, Pushover and email, and progress updates.

docs.title: Remote access
docs.text:
• off — only reachable on your home network.
  • on — share links that work from anywhere. See Remote access.

docs.title: Camera streamer
docs.text:
In 2) Change setup the installer first asks Use Printer Buddy's camera streamer? It replaces Crowsnest (or any camera service already on the printer). Answer No to keep what you have (the same as the old off), or Yes to pick a level:

  • light — USB cameras, MJPEG (mjpg-streamer).
  • basic — USB cameras, MJPEG (ustreamer).
  • advanced — everything above, plus Pi cameras, network cameras (RTSP / IP) and WebRTC (go2rtc); needs more CPU.

Then it asks where the camera is plugged in (this box or the printer). Any number of cameras at every level. The installer doesn't ask for network camera addresses. For network cameras on this box, put each address as device: in data/streamer.conf after the install.

If the camera is on the printer, the installer shows how to install the streamer there. See Camera streamer.

docs.title: Release channel
docs.text:
• stable — tested releases.
  • nightly — the newest builds, may have bugs.

You can also put single parts on nightly — see Dev/beta builds.

docs.title: Setting them without the menu
docs.text:
Every choice has a command-line flag:

./install.sh --ui advanced --ai basic --video timelapse --stream basic

docs.title: Reinstall, back up and uninstall
docs.text: Everything here is in the installer menu: run ./install.sh in the Printer Buddy folder.

docs.title: Reinstall
docs.text:
1) Reinstall runs the whole install again with your current setup. Your printers and settings are kept — they live in data/ and printer-buddy.env, which the installer never overwrites.

Use it if something got broken or after changing a lot by hand.

docs.title: Back up and restore
docs.text:
4) Backup / restore data

  • Back up copies data/ (your printers, layouts, timelapses, AI photos…) and printer-buddy.env into backups/<date-time>/.
  • Restore lists your backups, stops Printer Buddy, puts the chosen one back and starts it again. It replaces your current printers and settings, so it asks first.

Tip

Make a backup before big changes, and copy the backups/ folder somewhere else now and then.

docs.title: Uninstall
docs.text:
6) Uninstall stops and removes the Printer Buddy service. It then asks, one at a time, whether to also delete:

  • the Python environment (.venv)
  • your printers and settings (data/) — make a backup first if you're unsure

The Printer Buddy folder itself stays; delete it by hand if you want it gone completely.

docs.title: Updates
docs.text:
Printer Buddy is made of parts that update separately:

Part What it is Printer Buddy The core app Interface The web pages Notifications Alerts to ntfy, Discord, Telegram, Pushover and email Timelapse Timelapse recording Camera streamer Only if it's on AI model Only if AI is on

docs.title: The Updates list
docs.text: Open ☰ on the home page and scroll to Updates. Each part shows the installed version and, if there's a newer one, what it updates to. Under Printers you'll also find each printer's own updates (Klipper, Moonraker, Fluidd…) from its Moonraker update manager.

docs.title: Update and Update all
docs.text:
Update on a row updates that part; Update all does everything. Printer Buddy restarts when it's done and the page reloads by itself. Prints on the printers keep going.

Tier menus (Camera streamer tier, AI model) switch that part and download it straight away.

docs.title: Stable and nightly
docs.text:
• stable — tested releases with version numbers (like v1.2.5).
  • nightly — built every day from the newest code; may have bugs.

Stable is the default. Put a single part on nightly with Dev/beta builds.

docs.title: Waiting
docs.text: Sometimes a new version of a part needs a newer version of another part first. Its row then says needs … first and shows Waiting instead of Update. Update the part it names, and it'll be offered after.

docs.title: From the terminal
docs.text:
cd printer-buddy
./update.sh

Or run ./install.sh and pick 3) Update. The installer's Update also refreshes things the app can't do on its own (like Printer Buddy's root helper), so run it once if an update tells you to.

docs.title: Dev/beta builds
docs.text: You can try the newest build of one part while everything else stays stable.

docs.title: Switching one part
docs.text:
1. Open ☰ on the home page and scroll to Updates.
  2. Press and hold the part's name for half a second (or right-click it).
  3. Tick Dev/beta builds and confirm.

That part downloads its nightly build and Printer Buddy restarts. Parts on dev show an orange DEV tag.

Putting Printer Buddy itself on dev moves the core app to the newest code too.

docs.title: Going back
docs.text: Hold the name again and untick Dev/beta builds. The part goes back to its stable version.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
Warning

Dev builds are newer and haven't been tested as much. If something breaks, switch the part back to stable.

docs.title: AI failure detection
docs.text: Printer Buddy's own models look at the printer's camera during prints and score how likely each problem is.

docs.title: What it looks for
docs.text: Spaghetti, warping, first-layer problems, stringing, blobs, cracks and other failures.

docs.title: Models
docs.text:
Model Runs on Notes basic A Raspberry Pi (64-bit) Pick this on a Pi heavy A strong PC or a GPU The most accurate

64-bit only for now

The AI needs a 64-bit system (Raspberry Pi OS 64-bit, or any x86_64 PC). A 32-bit version of the lite model is planned (lite only).

NVIDIA GPU (nightly builds for now)

heavy can use an NVIDIA GPU. If the host has a working NVIDIA driver (nvidia-smi works), the installer sets up the GPU version of the AI libraries. The GPU also needs NVIDIA's CUDA and cuDNN libraries installed on the host; without them it runs on the CPU. Settings → AI shows what the model runs on.

Pick one with AI detection in the installer. Every model release is tested on the same 1,000 photos; the scores are in each release's notes under Model check. With the v1.5 models, basic is right 93% of the time and catches 91% of failures; heavy is right 95% of the time with only 3% false alarms.

docs.title: When it alerts
docs.text:
It checks the camera every few seconds while a printer prints, and only alerts after several checks in a row look bad, so one odd frame doesn't set it off. Change these in Settings → AI:

Setting Choices Default Alert when a problem scores at least 40-80% 60% Check the camera every 5, 10, 20, 30 s 10 s …for this many checks in a row 1, 2, 3, 5 3 Then wait before alerting again 5, 10, 20, 30 min 10 min

Higher threshold or more checks in a row = fewer false alarms, but a failure is caught a little later.

Per printer (AI watch on the printer page) you choose Alert only, Alert + auto-pause or Off.

docs.title: The failure box
docs.text: When the AI thinks something's wrong, a red box on the camera shows where. Box: on failure (default) only works it out when a failure is likely; Box: always draws it on every check (uses more CPU). Turn both off to save CPU on older Pis.

docs.title: Score history
docs.text: Click History in the AI watch section to see a chart of the highest problem score from each check during the current print. The dashed line is your alert threshold, and a red line marks each alert. It keeps up to 4,320 checks per print (12 hours at the default 10 s).

docs.title: Detection area
docs.text: By default the AI looks at the whole picture. To make it ignore clutter around the bed, click Detection area in the AI watch section and drag a box over the camera picture. Clear area goes back to the whole picture.

docs.title: Helping train it
docs.text:
• When it alerts, answer Was it really a failure? — false alarms are the most useful.
  • Save for AI… saves the current camera view with a label.
  • Settings → AI shows saved photos and how often the AI was right on your printers. Turn on Help improve the AI to send labelled photos for training.

docs.title: Camera streamer
docs.text: Printer Buddy's camera streamer is a replacement for crowsnest and camera-streamer. It streams your USB, Pi and network cameras and is set up, updated and controlled from Printer Buddy like every other part.

docs.title: Tiers
docs.text:
Tier What it does off Streamer not installed light USB cameras, MJPEG (mjpg-streamer) basic USB cameras, MJPEG (ustreamer) advanced Everything above, plus Pi cameras, network cameras (RTSP / IP) and WebRTC (go2rtc); needs more CPU

Any number of cameras at every level.

Pick it with Camera streamer in the installer's 2) Change setup. It first asks whether you want to use it at all, then a level, then where the camera is plugged in (see Install choices), or switch tiers in the Updates list (home page ☰). It runs as its own service, printer-buddy-streamer, which you can restart or stop from the home page ☰ drawer.

docs.title: Cameras
docs.text: Each printer's cameras come from Moonraker. On a printer page, the camera's settings let you add or edit Moonraker cameras, flip or rotate them and pick the main camera — the one the AI and timelapses use.

docs.title: On the printer
docs.text:
If the camera is plugged into the printer itself, run the streamer there. In Change setup pick Camera streamer, answer Yes, pick a level, then The printer. The installer offers two ways to install it:

  • Copy and paste — it shows one command to run over SSH on the printer, for example curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/printer-buddy/print-buddy-streamer/main/install-printer.sh | bash -s -- basic.
  • Guided SSH — it asks for the printer's IP and login user (default pi) and runs the same command over SSH. SSH asks for the printer's password; nothing is saved.

The installer doesn't ask for network camera addresses. Add each one as device: in the streamer's settings after the install, or give the addresses when you run the command by hand, after the level, for example ... | bash -s -- advanced rtsp://192.168.0.50/stream.

On the printer, the command installs what the level needs, downloads the streamer to ~/print-buddy-streamer, starts it as the printer-buddy-streamer service and adds the cameras to the printer's Moonraker. It's also added to Moonraker's update manager, so you can update and restart it from Fluidd or Mainsail. Its settings are in printer_data/config/print-buddy-streamer.conf.

Printer Buddy then sees the cameras through Moonraker like any other camera.

Note

The printer needs Debian-based Linux with apt and Python 3.9 or newer. A printer without apt can't run it; use the printer's own camera service there.

New

The printer install and the light level are new and have not been tested on a real printer yet.

Cameras start at port 8081 so they don't clash with Printer Buddy on 8080.

docs.title: It replaces Crowsnest
docs.text:
That's why the installer asks first. The streamer does the job of Crowsnest or any camera service already on the printer. The installer doesn't stop or remove the old service. If you switch to the streamer, stop the old one yourself so two camera services aren't running side by side.

Nightly for now

The first question (whether to use the streamer at all) is on nightly and comes to stable with the next release.

docs.title: Dashboard
docs.text: The home page shows every printer you've added.

docs.title: Printer cards
docs.text: Each card shows the printer's state (printing, paused, idle, offline, error), the file, progress, time left, nozzle and bed temperatures and the camera. Click a card to open its printer page.

docs.title: Views and sorting
docs.text:
• Sort by status, name, progress or your own order (drag the cards; advanced interface).
  • Search to filter by name.
  • List view and groups (advanced interface) for lots of printers.

docs.title: Quick View
docs.text: Open a printer in a pop-up without leaving the dashboard — handy for a quick look at the camera and progress.

docs.title: Editing the layout
docs.text: Edit layout lets you add, move, resize and remove panels on the home page, the same way as on printer pages.

docs.title: Top bar
docs.text:
• News (bell) — Printer Buddy news and notices from your printers (like Moonraker warnings).
  • Settings — alerts, AI, look and about.
  • ☰ — the Printer Buddy drawer: restart, host power, services and updates.
  • Add by IP and Scan network — add printers.

docs.title: ☰ drawers
docs.text: The ☰ button at the right of the top bar opens a drawer from the right. Click outside it, press Esc or × to close it. Everything asks before doing anything, and warns you if a print is running.

docs.title: On a printer page
docs.text:
For that printer:

  • Restart — Klipper, Firmware (MCU reset), Moonraker.
  • Host — Reboot or Shut down the printer's host.
  • Power — Moonraker power devices (only if the printer has any set up).
  • Services — every service Moonraker lists (Klipper, Moonraker…) with its state, Restart and Start/Stop.

docs.title: On the home page
docs.text:
For Printer Buddy's host (a printer or a dedicated host):

  • Restart — Printer Buddy. Prints keep going on the printers; the page reloads when it's back.
  • Host — Reboot or Shut down Printer Buddy's host.
  • Services — printer-buddy, and printer-buddy-streamer if the camera streamer is on.
  • Updates — see Updates.

docs.title: Notifications
docs.text: Printer Buddy can message you when something happens on a printer.

docs.title: Services
docs.text:
Service Needs ntfy basic Discord basic Telegram advanced Pushover advanced Email advanced

The advanced ones need Notifications = advanced in the installer.

docs.title: Events
docs.text: Started, paused, resumed, finished, failed, cancelled, went offline and Klipper shutdown — plus AI alerts. With advanced notifications you can also get progress updates (for example at 25% and 50%).

docs.title: Setting them up
docs.text:
1. Open Settings → Alerts.
  2. Add a service and fill in its details (ntfy topic, Discord webhook URL…).
  3. Tick the events you want.
  4. Send a test to check it works.

docs.title: Printer page
docs.text: Click a printer on the dashboard to open its page.

docs.title: Tabs and panels
docs.text:
The sidebar on the left holds the page's tabs. Each tab is made of panels (status, camera, temperatures, move, console, files, bed mesh, macros…).

  • Edit layout (top bar) lets you add, move and remove panels and tabs, and drag tabs to reorder them.
  • Collapse at the bottom of the sidebar shrinks it to icons.

docs.title: Camera
docs.text:
The camera panel shows the printer's main camera. Use the buttons in its top-right corner:

  • Full screen — fills the screen. Press the same button, or Esc, to leave.
  • + and − — zoom in and out, up to 8 times. You can also scroll the mouse wheel over the picture to zoom towards the cursor, or double-click to zoom to 2.5 times and double-click again to go back.
  • Moving around — when you're zoomed in, drag the picture. On a touch screen, drag with one finger and pinch with two.
  • The zoom button (for example 2.5×) appears while you're zoomed in. Click it to go back to normal. Switching camera or printer also resets the zoom.

It's a digital zoom: the page enlarges the picture the camera sends, so you don't get more detail than the camera gives you.

Nightly for now

Zoom, moving around and leaving full screen with the same button are on nightly and come to stable with the next release. Full screen itself works on stable too, and Esc always leaves it.

docs.title: Macros
docs.text:
The macros panel shows each of your printer's macros as a button.

  • Click a macro to run it. A macro that takes values has a small arrow next to it: click the arrow to open a box with a field for each value, then Send. The name button runs it without values.
  • Hide some… shows an × on each button so you can hide the ones you never use. Show hidden brings them back.
  • Organize… puts macros in groups you name, such as Calibration or Camera. Pick a group for each macro in the list. Click a group's heading to fold it.
  • Suggest groups (in Organize) sorts macros that aren't in a group yet, by their names, into Print, Calibration, Motion, Filament, Temperature, Camera, Lights and System. Macros that share a first word, such as MMU_LOAD and MMU_UNLOAD, go in a group named after it. Macros you've already grouped stay where they are.
  • Lock (in Organize) greys a macro out while a print is running or paused. An unlocked macro still asks you to confirm when you run it during a print.

Groups, locks and hidden macros are saved in your browser, for each printer.

Nightly for now

Groups, locks and the arrow for values are on nightly and come to stable with the next release.

docs.title: Job queue
docs.text:
The queue panel lines up prints to run one after another. Add files with + Queue in the Files panel. For each file you can set how many copies to print (− and +), move it to the front with ↑ Next, or remove it. Start queue and Pause queue control when the next job starts.

Under the list it adds up the queue: Filament (metres and grams), Print time and ETA, the time the whole queue should finish. If a print is running, the ETA includes what's left of it. If some files have no estimate in them, a note says how many.

Nightly for now

The filament, print time and ETA totals are on nightly and come to stable with the next release.

docs.title: Database backup
docs.text:
The Database backup panel (add it with Add a panel) backs up Moonraker's database, which holds your print history, spools and saved settings.

  • Create backup saves one, named with the date and time.
  • The restore button puts a backup back. It replaces everything in the database with that backup, so it asks first, and it's off while a print is running.
  • Compact database shrinks the database file.

Nightly for now

This panel is on nightly and comes to stable with the next release.

docs.title: Top bar
docs.text: Button What it does Save config Only shows when Klipper has unsaved changes — see below Theme Light or dark Pause / Cancel Pause or cancel the current print Emergency stop Stops the printer immediately ☰ The printer drawer: restarts, host power, services

docs.title: Console
docs.text:
Type G-code and press Send.

  • ↑ / ↓ go through the commands you've sent.
  • Start typing to get suggestions for every command and macro Klipper knows.
  • Filters hides lines you don't care about (like temperature reports).
  • Click a line you sent to put it back in the box.

docs.title: Klipper errors and warnings
docs.text:
When Klipper isn't ready, a red banner under the top bar says why — Klipper's own error (for example a config mistake and its line), or that Klipper isn't connected to Moonraker. It has Restart, Firmware restart, Restart service and a link to download klippy.log.

When Klipper is fine but there are warnings (deprecated config options, a Moonraker part that failed to start…), a yellow banner lists them. Hide hides it until the warnings change.

docs.title: Save config
docs.text: After a calibration, bed mesh, offset or anything else Klipper hasn't saved yet, an orange Save config button appears. Click it to see exactly what will be written to printer.cfg, then Save config & restart (runs SAVE_CONFIG, which restarts Klipper). It's disabled while printing.

docs.title: Remote access
docs.text: By default Printer Buddy only works on your home network. Remote access lets you check a printer from anywhere with a share link.

docs.title: Turning it on
docs.text:
Pick Remote access = on in 2) Change setup and go back. The installer then installs a secure tunnel (cloudflared), registers it and starts it.

Turn it off again and the installer asks whether to remove the tunnel. Share links stop working from outside once it's removed.

docs.title: Share links
docs.text:
Share a printer's view with someone else. Links look like:

https://www.printerbuddy.stream/share/user/<your id>/...

To make one, open the menu on a printer's card on the dashboard and choose Share. It only shows when remote access is on. Pick how long the link works:

  • 1 hour, 1 day or 7 days
  • until the print ends — only offered while a print is running. The link turns itself off when the print finishes, is cancelled or fails.
  • until I turn it off

Untick Chat if you want a link with no chat box at all. Then Create link, and Copy it. The list shows each link and when it stops working, and Turn off ends one straight away.

The people you send it to see the printer's camera, progress, time left, layer and temperatures. They can't control anything. On the page, the full screen button in the corner of the camera fills the screen (double-click does the same) and the same button leaves it.

docs.title: Chat
docs.text:
Everyone watching a printer through a share link can chat. The page has a Chat button next to the printer's name: click it to open the chat box, and click it again to close it. Each viewer types a name (it's remembered in their browser) and a message, and everyone watching that printer sees it, whichever of your links they used.

You see the same chat in the Share window in Printer Buddy and can write in it as Owner. Clear chat empties it for everyone. The Allow chat tickbox there switches chat on or off for that printer: it's on by default, and turning it off hides the Chat button on every share link for that printer and clears the chat.

  • A link made with Chat unticked never shows the chat button, and the list marks it "no chat".
  • Messages are plain text, up to 300 characters, one every 2 seconds per viewer.
  • The last 100 messages are kept in memory. They're gone when Printer Buddy restarts.
  • A link that's turned off or has expired loses the chat too.

docs.title: Push notifications
docs.text:
Open Alerts and blocked words in the chat part of the Share window and pick Notify me with a push. It uses the notification service you set up in Settings.

  • Never: chat stays quiet. You only see it when you open the window.
  • Only when a viewer flags the print (the default).
  • For every message: at most one push every 20 seconds, saying how many more came in.

docs.title: Flag button
docs.text: Next to Send, viewers have a Flag button for when they spot something the AI missed. It asks them to confirm, then sends you a push with a camera picture, using whatever they typed (up to 100 characters) as the reason. The flag also shows in the chat. Flags always push unless alerts are set to Never. A viewer can flag once a minute, and a printer takes at most 5 flags in 10 minutes.

docs.title: Blocked words
docs.text:
The same section has a list of words that aren't allowed, one per line. A message or name containing one is refused and the viewer is told so, and they can't send or flag anything for 10 seconds. You see the attempt in your chat window, in grey, with the name and what they typed. Other viewers never see it, and you aren't sent a push for it. It's saved in chat-blocklist.txt next to the database, so you can edit that file instead if you prefer. On top of your list, a built-in list of common swear words, insults and slurs is blocked. Untick Also block the built-in list to turn it off. It can't catch every spelling, and it only blocks whole words, so ordinary words like "class" or "assist" are fine.

  • word blocks that whole word only, two words blocks the phrase.
  • word* blocks any word that starts with it, *word any word that ends with it, and *word* blocks it anywhere, even inside other words.
  • Capitals, accents, look-alikes (1 for i, 0 for o, @ for a) and spaces between letters (b a d) are caught.

Nightly for now

Chat is on nightly and comes to stable with the next release. For viewers coming in through remote access, the relay also has to be updated, which happens when its repository is pushed.

docs.title: Who can see what
docs.text: There's no login. Each share link has its own long, secret code, and anyone with the link can see that printer, so only send it to people you trust. Links can be set to expire, and you can delete a link any time to stop it working.

docs.title: Turning it on
docs.text: Pick Video = timelapse in the installer. It installs ffmpeg, which makes the videos.

docs.title: How it records
docs.text:
Setting Choices Default Mode every layer, or every few seconds every layer Interval (interval mode) seconds between frames 10 s Frame rate frames per second in the video 25 Keep how many timelapses to keep per printer 20

A timelapse starts with the print and the video is made when it ends. Prints with fewer than two frames don't make a video.

docs.title: Finding your videos
docs.text: Open the printer's Timelapses tab to watch, download or delete them. They're stored in Printer Buddy's data/ folder.
